Theme

Latin word

cōgō

cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; of animals, people, fruit

round up, drive together, collect; force, compel

In this lexicon

  • collect

    also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 5.2.15: cōgantur (ovēs) intrō (Lewis & Short); Cato Agr. 64.1: oleam (cōgere), to gather (Lewis & Short); Traupman 107: round up, cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum; Traupman 320

  • force

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 780–781: coāctus lēgibus eam uxōrem dūcet; Verg. Ecl. 2.7: morī mē dēnique cōgēs?; Traupman 317

Examples

  • nīl nostrī miserēre? morī mē dēnique cōgēs?

    have you no pity for me? will you drive me to my death in the end?Verg. Ecl. 2.7

    In the entry for force

  • hujus igitur bellī ego particeps et socius et adjūtor esse cōgor …?

    am I, then, to be forced to be a partner, an ally and a helper in this war …?Cic. Att. 9.10.5

    In the entry for force

  • Coāctus lēgibus eam uxōrem dūcet.

    The law will force him to marry her.Ter. And. 780–781
